title: Result Day
hook: Every semester your university result site dies at 10:00 sharp, when 300,000 students check their marks within a couple of minutes. This time you own the fix.
context: University results portal, 300,000 students, results published once per semester at a fixed time.
solution_brief: Precompute result pages privately, require each student to authenticate before access, and only then serve their own result through a private cache or short-lived authorized response. Stage the release ahead of time and switch it at publication. Use origin shielding for shared assets, rate limits for abuse, and never treat a roll number or date of birth as authorization.

steps.prompt: Every result view runs SELECT marks FROM results WHERE roll_no = ?, and the database falls over at 10:00. The results never change after publication. What is the best fundamental change?
steps.context_note: The traffic is a huge spike, but the data is immutable once published.

options.text: Buy a much bigger database server and keep running the same lookup for every view
Add read replicas and keep running the same query for every view
Precompute each result and serve it behind per-student authorization
Cache the query output at the CDN under a URL built from the roll number

steps.explanation: Immutable data can be computed once and served many times, as long as each result stays private behind a per-student check. A bigger server or more replicas still run one query per view and face the same spike, while a public cache keyed by roll number lets anyone who guesses a number read that student's marks.
steps.bottleneck_note: If data cannot change, you should not compute it at request time.

steps.prompt: Results must not need a marks query per view, yet each student may see only their own. How should the precomputed results be laid out and served?
steps.context_note: Static serving is the plan, but each result is personal.

options.text: One private object per student, served only after checking who is signed in
One file holding all 300,000 results, downloaded and searched in the browser
One public object per student at a URL built from the roll number
One page per department listing every student's marks behind a shared password

steps.explanation: Small per-student objects remove the live query while keeping the store private, with the sign-in check in front of every response. One big download hands every student everyone's marks, and public or shared-password pages expose results to anyone who guesses a URL or learns the password.
steps.bottleneck_note: Precomputation changes the serving path, not the need for authorization.

steps.prompt: How do you make the results visible at exactly 10:00 without exposing them early or doing the heavy upload at the last moment?
steps.context_note: The private files can be built ahead of time, but nothing may be visible before 10:00.

options.text: Upload everything at 10:00:00 and let the upload finish as fast as it can
Protect the files with a shared password announced at 10:00
Publish them early under an unlisted URL and tell nobody until 10:00
Stage the files ahead of time and flip a release pointer at 10:00

steps.explanation: Preparing and publishing are separate jobs: the heavy upload happens early and privately, and publishing becomes one cheap atomic switch, with the per-student check in front before and after. Uploading at 10:00 risks partial availability, and unlisted URLs or shared passwords are not real access control.
steps.bottleneck_note: Separate 'prepare' from 'publish'. Publishing should be one cheap atomic switch.

steps.prompt: Which change keeps this cold-cache burst from reaching the origin thousands of times?
steps.context_note: At 10:00:00 thousands of students request the same page shell and release manifest, and all of them miss the CDN cache together.

options.text: Lower the CDN cache lifetime to one second so content is refreshed constantly
Add origin shielding with request coalescing for shared assets
Add more origin servers behind the CDN to absorb the burst
Have browsers retry failed requests straight away

steps.explanation: Shielding and coalescing collapse many simultaneous misses for the same shared asset into a single origin fetch, and pre-warming helps further. A shorter cache lifetime creates more misses, and immediate browser retries amplify the burst. Extra origin servers absorb load but do not remove the duplicate fetches. None of this merges private per-student results, which are different objects.
steps.bottleneck_note: Caches fail hardest on a cold start. Plan the first second, not just the steady state.

steps.prompt: Students refresh every second, and a scraper requests roll numbers 1 to 400000 to collect everyone's marks. Which protection handles both?
steps.context_note: The site is standing, and now two kinds of heavy traffic arrive: nervous students and a scraper.

options.text: Rely on the data being static, because nothing about it can be changed by traffic
Block all traffic from outside the university's own network and VPN
Check the signed-in student on every request and rate limit at the edge
Ask for roll number and date of birth on each result lookup

steps.explanation: A signed-in identity check stops one student requesting another's result, private origin storage prevents bypassing it, and edge rate limits blunt both refresh storms and enumeration. Roll numbers and dates of birth are guessable, so they identify a person without proving it is them, and blocking off-campus traffic locks out students at home.
steps.bottleneck_note: Never use a guessable URL or personal attribute as proof of access.
